title: PipelineResult gains an error channel, layered in the engine
description: A run whose commit was refused must not report that it succeeded. Add errors to PipelineResult and populate it from the interpreter's failures -- which PgeEngine.run currently discards, with a comment saying so. This deliberately revises a surface the previous spec froze; that revision is authorised, and the docs/pge-graph.md disposition it changes is updated in the same commit.

successCriteria.description: PipelineResult declares errors?: readonly PipelineFailure[]; PipelineFailure carries nodeId, branchKey, errorClass and message, mapped 1:1 from TaskFailure minus superstep.

The array is layered in PgeEngine.run, NOT inside finalizePipelineRun, by removing the discard at src/pge/engine/pge-engine.ts:461-475 -- mirroring how RunResultFlusher.flush layers needsClarification with a spread after finalization.
The frozen key-order test in src/orchestrator/finalize.test.ts stays green, unmodified.

A PgeEngine run whose git-effect commit node is refused FAIL_CLOSED under the autopilot noop mechanism returns a non-empty errors array whose first entry has nodeId "commit" and an errorClass naming the refusal.
A TsPipelineEngine run returns a result with no errors key, and `success` keeps the shared deriveRunSuccess formula on both engines -- Option A semantics, per the spec's D3 decision.
docs/pge-graph.md's engine-migration disposition and the sprint-13 recorded limitation are rewritten to state that the error channel now exists, in this commit.
Full suite, typecheck, typecheck:tests, lint and build are green.

nonGoals: Setting success:false on a fail-closed refusal -- explicitly Option B, out of scope, and it would add completionMarker to the divergence set.
Changing deriveRunSuccess, the runPipeline signature, or the completion marker.
Surfacing the errors in the CLI or MCP layers -- that is sprint 6.
Re-capturing golden cases -- that is sprint 8, deliberately separated so the diff is read on its own.
stopConditions: Adding the optional field breaks a consumer that cannot be fixed within this sprint -- stop, list the consumers, and report.
conformance.engines.test.ts's divergence set changes as a side effect -- stop; a change to that pin must be deliberate and separately justified.
definitionOfDone: All required criteria met, the full suite plus typecheck, typecheck:tests, lint and build are green, and every documentation claim added is backed by a test that fails when the claim stops being true.
generatorNotes: Read src/orchestrator/workflow/flusher.ts:113-127 first -- it is the exact pattern, and its comment explains WHY engine-specific fields are layered after finalizePipelineRun rather than inside it: so the two engines cannot disagree about the shared fields. Follow it literally. The discard you are removing is at src/pge/engine/pge-engine.ts:461-475 and its own comment tells you what it was waiting for. Keep errors OPTIONAL so every existing consumer of PipelineResult keeps compiling; enumerate those consumers before you start. Do not widen the sprint split to absorb a terminal-node failure -- that would invent a failed sprint that did not happen, which the discarded comment warns against explicitly.
evaluatorNotes: Two things to check hard. First, that the field really is layered in the engine and not in finalize: read finalizePipelineRun and confirm it is untouched, and confirm finalize.test.ts's key-order pin was not edited. Second, that the ts engine is genuinely unaffected -- run one and assert 'errors' in result is false, not merely that it is undefined. Then check the conformance divergence set is still exactly the four fields; if a fifth appeared, that is a stop condition and must be reported, not accepted. Finally verify the docs update actually replaces the old claim rather than appending a contradicting paragraph next to it.
